Samira — thanks for the quick heads-up and the log dump, very helpful. We're on it. Immediate notes & next steps: 

1) Triage (now): I kicked a high-priority investigation with the runtime on-call to look for queue/backpressure signals (queue length, active tokens, scheduler stalls).
2) Short-term mitigation (applied at 09:45 PST):
   - Reduced concurrency cap for AtlasAI's dedicated pool from 120 -> 80 to lower queuing pressure.
   - Enabled KV-prefetch (prefix cache warm) for your tenant for requests that share session prefixes.
   - Added a temporary routing rule to favor the cheaper-latency variant (redwood-v2-xl-quant) for non-critical calls.
3) Ask of you: can you confirm whether you saw the same errors for both streaming and non-streaming calls?
4) Timeline: we expect to see the immediate change in tail metrics within 15-30 minutes; deeper RCA and a short exec summary by 16:00 PST.

I'll attach a short mitigation note once we confirm improvement. Looping Laura/Marissa for visibility and for any account-level communications.

- Rohan

Samira — quick update from the on-call triage and what we did (attached mitigation_report_20260801.pdf):

Observations (preliminary):
- Concurrency buildup visible on the request scheduler coincident with a small rollout of a kernel-change on a subset of nodes (kernel v3.7.1). A minority of backends hit degraded allocator behavior that increased per-request dispatch time by ~30-40ms, which at high concurrency amplified into p99 spikes.
- We also saw an increased token fanout on several sessions, which amplified KV-cache misses and led to spurts of longer tail latencies.
- Error bursts (5xx) appear correlated with short-lived OOM throttles on the affected hosts.

Immediate actions taken at 09:45 PST:
- Reduced concurrency cap for AtlasAI pool: 120 -> 80.
- Drained and quarantined affected kernels; rolled back kernel v3.7.1 on the impacted nodes to v3.6.9.
- Enabled a stricter per-connection token limit to prevent long-running cross-session spikes.
- Route failover: traffic to the fallback quantized variant for non-critical endpoints.

Impact: within 20 minutes we observed p99 drop from ~3.6s -> ~1.4s and error rate dropped to baseline. We are continuing to monitor.

Next steps (RCA):
- Deep post-mortem comparing kernel-change batches and allocator telemetry (owner: Runtime team).
- Workload-specific guidance: recommend AtlasAI reduce max-session token window or enable stricter prefix caching for hot sessions (owner: Customer Reliability / Solutions).
- Exec summary & timeline: will deliver a 1-page exec note + post-mortem draft by 15:30 PST.

Attachment: mitigation_report_20260801.pdf (short log snippets and metric charts).

Suggested meeting: 11:30 PST bridge for walk-through; link will be in calendar.

Thanks,
Rohan
